9e0d922f8dd5cbb0: PARIS: Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan on Thursday to make it three wins from their opening three games in the Europa League.
Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth firmly in control against AC Milan, one of Europe's leading clubs.
Milan goalkeeper and skipper Mike Maignan was red carded early on for a foul on Tyler Adams and his side never fully recovered.

Amine Adli scored a sublime 84th free-kick to make it 3-0, the Premier League side having opened their inaugural Europa League campaign with victory at Real Sociedad followed by a 3-0 home win over Sturm Graz last week.
Bournemouth, who became the first English club since Sunderland in 1973/74 to win the first three European fixtures in their history, will now face Sparta Prague and Celta Vigo in November.
"It means a lot. We came off two victories, so that gave us a good feeling for this game," Kluivert told TNT Sports.
"We trust ourselves. It doesn't matter who we play against. We know what we're capable of, and I think we showed that today."

Bournemouth's Premier League rivals Crystal Palace rebounded from a 5-0 weekend thrashing by Brighton to claim a 2-2 draw with Beskitas in Istanbul, while Scottish giants Celtic suffered a third successive defeat, going down 2-1 to Celta Vigo.
Bayer Leverkusen, however, also made it three straight wins with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday's third matchday.

The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium's Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be'er Sheva.
Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games.
Juventus thought they had come from behind to beat French side Rennes but had their late 'winner' ruled out for a marginal offside.
Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead.
Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi's 88th minute strike.
Clad in a new all-pink kit, Sunderland were left kicking themselves after a 1-1 draw in Poland.
The Blacks Cats took a second minute lead in Poznan thanks to Timur Tutierov and dominated the game without being able to close out the win.
With two home games remaining, however, the second round still beckons for Regis Le Bris' side.
Marseille went down 1-0 to Sturn Graz while Lyon suffered a 3-0 thrashing at the hands of Hoffenheim.
In the Conference League, former Liverpool striker Mohamed Salah opened the scoring from the penalty spot in Trabzonspor's 2-0 win over Scottish side Hearts.
Brighton were held to a 0-0 draw at Czech side Jablonec, as Monaco thumped Freiburg 3-0 and Ajax snuck a 2-0 win over Atalanta.

11fc5fbdf699a1cf: AUSTIN: Kimi Antonelli admitted on Thursday that he needs to have a 'perfect weekend' at the United States Grand Prix to realise his dream of winning a maiden drivers' world championship.

Mercedes' 20-year-old Italian could become the youngest champion in F1 history and the first from Italy since Alberto Ascari in 1953 if he wins Sunday's race and nearest rival and team-mate George Russell fails to finish in the top eight.
He would also need seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari to finish outside the top four.
"If you think about it, it's crazy," said a smiling and relaxed Antonelli, speaking to reporters at a news conference at the Circuit of the Americas.
"For me, it needs to be a perfect weekend and the others they need to do a poor result, which is unlikely.
"Of course, anything can happen and it's crazy to think about it. We had a meeting this morning and we said 'just have fun' so we're in the same mindset that I've had all year.
"So, we go one race at a time and I just try to do my best every weekend and then we'll see."
Seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton, who vacated his seat at Mercedes for Antonelli when he moved to Ferrari, warmly praised him for his talent and his general demeanour.
Asked, as a multiple champion, if he had any advice to give the young Italian who is on the brink of glory, Hamilton smiled and said: "Slow down!"
bce83c5d75aa2f06: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday declared imports of wind turbines and their components a threat to national security, but stopped short of imposing new tariffs on the sector.

In a White House proclamation, Trump said a Commerce Department investigation found that imported wind turbines threatened national security because of cybersecurity concerns linked to foreign-made equipment, interference with radar systems and air traffic operations, and increased US reliance on goods made overseas.

The move follows a probe launched in August 2025 under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act. It is one of numerous trade investigations the administration has conducted into the national security implications of imports across a range of sectors.
Instead of imposing immediate trade restrictions, Trump directed trade officials to pursue negotiations with trading partners and report back within 180 days.
Additional trade measures, including tariffs, could be considered later, the order said.
The order reiterates Trump's longstanding criticism of wind energy as unreliable because of its intermittent nature.
"Given wind energy's intermittent reliability, use of wind energy diverts the United States electrical grid from more reliable energy sources," the order said.
Major suppliers of wind turbines and components to the US include Mexico, France, India, Denmark and Germany, according to trade data cited by the centre-right think tank American Action Forum.
A spokesperson for the American Clean Power Association, a trade group representing clean energy companies, was not immediately available for comment.
a1e66a55733f67d9: BELGRADE: Around 150,000 supporters of Serbia's opposition student movement rallied in central Belgrade on Thursday, seeking to oust the party of veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic in a pivotal parliamentary election this weekend.
The Student List, a leaderless movement of student-backed candidates, wants to end more than 14 years of rule by Vucic's right-wing populist Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in Sunday's vote.

It poses the biggest threat Vucic has faced, and civil society groups have warned that the election campaign has been marred by intimidation, arrests, attacks, misuse of public resources and a distorted media environment.

"I came to support the Student List because young people finally gave me hope that it is possible to live in a normal country," 47-year-old Marija Nedeljkovic Radic told AFP as she arrived for the rally.
"Really, for the first time in my life, I believe that it is possible."
Around 150,000 people gathered at the Student List rally in Belgrade on Thursday evening, according to the independent crowd-monitoring group Archive of Public Gatherings in a post on X.
The vote comes after nearly two years of student-led protests sparked by the 2024 collapse of a canopy at the newly renovated Novi Sad railway station, which killed 16 people.
The tragedy, widely blamed on corruption, triggered some of Serbia's largest protests since the fall of strongman Slobodan Milosevic in 2000.
The anti-corruption movement, led by university students, grew from demands for a transparent investigation into the tragedy into calls for an early election.

Waving "Students are winning" flags, chanting and blowing whistles, students and their supporters marched through Belgrade before converging on Slavija Square, the site of some of their biggest protests.
They filled the square and surrounding streets, according to AFP reporters.

"We are putting an end to 14 years of humiliation, chaos and betrayal, and to decades of putting personal and party interests above yours," university professor Jugoslav Gasic, one of 250 candidates on the Student List, told the crowd, which chanted "Victory, victory!"
"You deserve better, and we know how to deliver it. Students are winning!"
The rally ended with the candidates stepping down from the stage into the crowd, holding the Serbian constitution and dancing a traditional folk dance with supporters.
Vucic defiant
Vucic has dominated Serbian politics for more than a decade, serving as either prime minister or president.
Amid mounting pressure, Vucic announced the snap election last month, setting up his biggest electoral challenge since his party took power in 2012.
Vucic, who addressed supporters at a sports hall in the capital on Thursday, has regularly accused the student movement of being a foreign-funded coup attempt.
"Let us never forget how they tried to bring down our state. Let us always protect and defend it," said the 56-year-old, who resigned to run for prime minister.
"Let us go out and defeat them! Defeat them decisively!" he said before white ticker tape and balloons showered the crowd.
Many of the 250 candidates on the Student List running for the 250-seat parliament are drawn from academia or are deliberate political outsiders.
The movement has a broad platform, but its core pledge is to fight corruption.
Serbia lacks reliable independent polling, and surveys have produced widely differing results.

Political scientist Dusan Vucicevic of Belgrade University told AFP it was difficult to predict the outcome but expected the students to win more than 40 per cent of the vote, a result significantly higher than that of any opposition list since the SNS came to power.
Threats, intimidation
Days before the vote, Serbian civil society groups warned that conditions for "free and fair elections" were lacking.
"This assessment is not based on isolated incidents, opposition claims or political disagreement with the government," a joint statement by 24 organisations said.
"It is supported by documented findings from independent Serbian organisations working in different fields."
On Wednesday, Belgrade prosecutors questioned six people arrested on suspicion of plotting "violence, riots and attacks" on election day.
Reports of threats and intimidation targeting student demonstrators have grown in recent months, but their rallies have remained largely peaceful since they began.
"I've been following this fight since the very beginning," 35-year-old rally attendee Igor said.
"Today is the last rally, and it's important that we all come here to send a message of love and peace and that we see each other on the 25th at the polling stations."

931883da1620ea4a: MOSCOW: Russian president Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that future talks on a settlement of the war in Ukraine should focus on security guarantees for both countries and an overall framework for security throughout Europe.
Putin, interviewed on Russian television a day after meeting US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff, confirmed that Russia was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month.
He restated longstanding Kremlin policy that Russia never wanted to launch a war, but had run into hostile reactions from Ukraine on key issues of concern to Moscow.
Talks on a variety of matters could lead to a positive outcome, he said, but Russia remained intent on a solution ending the conflict rather than a short-lived ceasefire.

"The goal of these talks will be to ensure the security of Ukraine and Russia after reaching peace agreements, in their final form, not as a result of a temporary ceasefire for some short period of time. We are ready to resume these contacts to achieve this goal," Putin said.

The Russian president said Witkoff also stressed that discussions had to extend to "the architecture of European security as a whole. And I agree with that too. Well, let's see how things develop in the coming days."

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who met Witkoff in Norway on Tuesday, said Ukraine was ready for talks likely to take place by early next month. Ukraine, he said, supported "any proposals for a ceasefire, an end to the war, an energy ceasefire as well as humanitarian initiatives".
Efforts headed by the US to pursue talks stalled in February with the outbreak of the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.
Many of the Ukraine war issues focus on territory, with Russia demanding Ukraine cede all of eastern Ukraine's Donbas region. Kyiv rejects any notion of giving up land it currently holds.
In his comments, Putin said any discussion on territory in eastern Ukraine had to consider what he said was the fact that the area was "historically Russian land".
Residents there, he said, had voted to be a part of Russia in referendums staged seven months after Moscow launched its invasion.
"Firstly, my attitude on this matter is that this is not their territory. It’s the territory of historical Russia," he said.
6d69531832d9c5a1: OTTAWA: A fast-moving grass fire that killed at least four soldiers at a western Canadian military base on Saturday was sparked by an exercise using live grenades, a senior defence official said on Thursday.
High winds then propelled the blaze across the army base in Wainwright, overwhelming dozens of soldiers. The incident was one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military.

"The fire initiated on the automatic grenade launcher range ... (it) initiated as a result of routine military training that was happening on that range at the time," Brigadier-General Vanessa Hanrahan told reporters.

Officials said 27 people remain hospitalised, several in critical condition. The soldiers and reserve members were preparing to deploy to Latvia, where Canadian forces have their largest international military operation.

f79aeece68c73f8a: ROTTERDAM: Japan’s Daiki Hashimoto successfully defended his men’s individual all-around title at the Artistic Gymnastics World Championships in Rotterdam on Thursday ahead of China’s Yang Haonan and Britain's Joe Fraser.
Having already claimed team gold the previous day, the 25-year-old from Narita secured his seventh world title in the Netherlands and his fourth all-around crown in a row.
He took it by a comfortable margin, finishing 1.799pts ahead of Yang. It was the biggest winning margin in a men's all-around at an Olympics or a worlds in 13 years.
Hashimoto is a worthy successor to fellow Japanese, the elegant Kohei Uchimura, who won a record six consecutive world all-around titles between 2009 and 2015.

Initially trailing the unflappable Yang, and despite a modest start on the first two apparatuses (floor exercise and rings), the three-time Olympic champion eventually surged to victory thanks to two outstanding performances on the parallel bars and the horizontal bar.
Reigning Olympic champion Shinnosuke Oka, meanwhile, endured a difficult evening. Two botched landings on vault during the fourth rotation ended his hopes of reaching the podium.
There was even greater disappointment for Russia’s Arsenii Dukhno, who trailed Hashimoto by just one-tenth of a point heading into the final rotation.
A fall on the horizontal bar following a missed grip ended his challenge for gold and even knocked him off the podium altogether, leaving him seventh.
The World Championships continue on Thursday with the women’s individual all-around competition.

MUNICH: Declan Rice scored a late equaliser to help last season's runners-up Arsenal grab a 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for Arsenal after coming on for the injured Bukayo Saka, but Alphonso Davies brought Bayern level after a sublime pass from Harry Kane.
Kane put Bayern on track for victory by converting a second-half penalty, but his England teammate Rice equalised with eight minutes remaining to earn Arsenal a point.
The Gunners have seven points from three games, two more than Bayern.
"We looked dangerous, we got the goal, and we had a moment there where we could have killed off the game," said Kane.
"Probably a draw was a fair result overall, so we take the point and move on."
The England captain posed a consistent threat against Arsenal's miserly defence with another excellent performance ahead of next week's Ballon d'Or ceremony in Kane's London hometown.
Kane's second-half penalty, his 16th goal in 23 matches against Arsenal, extended his scoring streak to 10 straight Champions League games.
Kane is one shy of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored in 11 consecutive matches for Real Madrid.

"I had an amazing season last year. I'm extremely proud of it. Winning the Ballon d'Or would be amazing. However, there's nothing I can do. The voting closed a long time ago, and I have to wait for the night and see what happens," Kane said of the award.
The draw was just the second time Arsenal had dropped points in 12 games in all competitions this season.
Meanwhile, Mikel Arteta said the club was "concerned" about winger Bakayo Saka's injury.
Saka, Arsenal's joint top goalscorer this season alongside Victor Gyokeres, went off early after falling to the turf, grabbing his thigh and was replaced by Eze.
"They are a bit concerned about Saka. When a player has to come off with sharp pain, it is never good news. We have to wait and see," Arteta said.

Actor Zul Ariffin has taken being overlooked for nominations at the 35th Malaysia Film Festival in his stride.
He believes that while accolades are always welcome for any performer, chasing trophies has never been for him.
Speaking at a film premiere in Kuala Lumpur recently, Zul said his main focus is on delivering strong performances and taking on quality projects.
He said that while being nominated for an award is a blessing, missing out does not bother him at all.
With this grounded mindset, the seasoned actor is thankful for the roles he is offered and the support from fans, especially with so many fresh faces entering the scene.
Looking ahead, he has his sights on several projects next year.
Zul cautioned that putting too much hope in awards can easily lead to disappointment, as major ceremonies only happen once a year.
He prefers to focus on quietly refining his craft.
He also paid tribute to the unsung heroes behind the camera, highlighting that production crews work far harder than the cast and deserve praise.
Zul won awards at the festival's 26th and 31st editions. His lack of nominations this time has raised eyebrows among fans, particularly as four films he was in had scored nominations.
3f5ae495107699ef: NEW YORK: US stocks tumbled on Thursday and the Nasdaq posted its steepest daily drop since early June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race.

The S&P 500 ended deep in negative territory. But the tech-laden Nasdaq, dragged down by microchips, suffered a steeper loss, falling 2.6% in the wake of a spate of high-profile AI-related earnings results.
The blue-chip Dow eked out a nominal gain minutes before the closing bell.

Meta Platforms' results beat analyst expectations, but its stock slid 7.0% as the Facebook parent posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade due to its AI-related expenditures and announced plans to issue non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise capital to spend on the nascent technology.
Tesla shares fell 3.1% even though the electric car maker unexpectedly posted positive free cash flow in the quarter and cut its 2026 capital spending plans.
The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index, which has driven much of the current bull market's gains, plunged 6.7%, its biggest daily percentage drop since June 23.
With Thursday's decline, the SOX is off more than 26% from its record closing high reached on June 22, yet it remains up 51.5% so far this year.
The S&P 500 has risen 11.9% over the same period.
"It's a wonderful day on Wall Street," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser & market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois.
"The only part of the market that is really suffering here is technology, which has been the golden child of the markets up until about June".

"Investors are starting to realise that there are some holes in the AI story," Nolte added. "And that's having an impact on the indices because they're so heavily weighted toward technology," he said.
On the geopolitical stage, Iran-backed Houthis launched new strikes against Saudi targets, sending crude prices to a five-month high.
Investors worried that ongoing Middle East strife could keep inflation hot and force the US Federal Reserve to keep raising interest rates.
Data from the Labor department showed initial claims for unemployment benefits kept drifting along near multi-decade lows.
Signs of labor market stability will allow the Fed to focus on fighting inflation.
Financial markets are currently pricing in the probability that the central bank will raise its policy rate by another 25 basis points before year-end.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 11.89 points, or 0.02%, to 52,867.98, the S&P 500 lost 93.74 points, or 1.21%, to 7,663.43 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 694.00 points, or 2.60%, to 26,008.86.
Third-quarter earnings season is well underway, with 111 of the companies in the S&P 500 having reported. Of those, 83% have beaten analyst expectations, according to the most recent LSEG data.
Procter & Gamble warned that rising cost pressures would take an increasing bite out of profit, but beat analyst estimates, sending the stock 5.6% higher and supporting consumer staples.
Blackstone advanced 8.4%, after the company said widening credit spreads on AI-related debt could present an opportunity to lock in higher returns.
Lockheed Martin climbed 7.0% after the aerospace/defense firm raised its annual sales and profit forecast.
Spotify rose 11.1% after the Swedish music streaming firm forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates, betting on its AI-powered features to drive user growth.
Union Pacific gained 3.6% following the company's quarterly earnings beat, which was helped by core pricing gains, although the railroad flagged a hit from rising fuel prices.
Chipmakers Intel, AMD, Sandisk and Marvell all tumbled more than 8% amid the broader semiconductor selloff.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.01-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 173 new highs and 366 new lows on the NYSE.
On the Nasdaq, 2,022 stocks rose and 2,766 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.37-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 40 new 52-week highs and four new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 82 new highs and 342 new lows.
Volume on US exchanges was 18.79 billion shares, compared with the 17.19 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

Police have named 11 corporations as suspects in ongoing investigations into forest and land fires, three of which are foreign-invested firms, according to the Antara news agency.
National police chief General Suyudi Ario Seto declined to name the companies but said the investigations were proceeding without major obstacles.
He told reporters following a plenary Cabinet meeting at the Presidential Palace complex here on Wednesday that accountability would extend beyond the corporate entities.
"This includes both company owners and shareholders who bear responsibility for the corporations linked to forest and land fires in Indonesia," said Suyudi.

The report said the criminal proceedings followed an earlier announcement by the National Police's Criminal Investigation Agency, which said it had raised 98 police reports concerning corporate-linked forest fires to the formal investigation stage.
Alongside the police investigations, the Forestry Ministry has stepped up administrative enforcement.
Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni said permits for six more companies in Central Kalimantan had been suspended, bringing the total number of forestry firms sanctioned to 32, according to the report.
The six companies had their Forest Utilisation Business Permits suspended and were ordered to undertake environmental restoration in affected areas.
Together, they hold concessions covering 201,391ha, of which 7,531ha were affected by recent fires.
The ministry's administrative sanctions now cover 32 companies managing more than 1.9 million hectares of concessions, including 18,489ha affected by fires.

KUALA LUMPUR: TNG Digital Sdn Bhd's GOfinance platform has recorded more than five million distinct investment users and processed RM3.57 billion in investment value as of Sept 30.

The financial services hub, available through TNG eWallet, offers a range of investment products, including money market funds, Amanah Saham, unit trusts, retirement solutions, digital gold and shares in local and overseas markets.
Selected products allow users to start investing with as little as RM10 and explore options that match their financial goals and risk appetite.
TNG Digital chief financial services officer Desmond Teoh said accessibility meant more than lowering minimum investment amounts; users also needed convenient access to a range of investment options.
"We recognise that trust matters when people make decisions about their money. Our aim is to give users a practical starting point and access to options as their financial needs change," he said.
The company said more than 4.7 million users had invested in GO+, while over 700,000 had traded digital gold through e-Mas.
TNG Digital said the figure represented unique users, with each user counted only once even if they had accessed multiple wealth products.
The company operates an open-platform model that connects its user base with established, regulated financial institutions and specialist partners to broaden access to investment products.
TNG Digital's partnerships have expanded the investment options available through TNG eWallet. Its collaboration with Webull, announced on Sept 30, introduced access to global share trading.

Malaysians can use the Malaysian Community Multiscale Air Quality Model (MyCMAQ) to check air pollution forecasts up to five days ahead.

Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the system, developed by the Meteorological Department, provided high-resolution forecasts of air quality and atmospheric pollutant concentrations in Malaysia and other parts of Southeast Asia.

"I hope the public will refer to this platform so they can make preparations and take the necessary action for activities over the next five days," he said during Ministers' Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
He was responding to Datuk Dr Richard Rapu @ Aman Begri (GPS-Betong), who asked about measures taken to ensure accurate and timely air quality information amid the current haze situation.
Arthur said the system was designed to provide more responsive air quality forecasts and haze warnings that were easier for the public to understand.
He added that the 68 automatic air quality monitoring stations operated by the Department of Environment monitored six major air pollutants continuously.

"These stations use measurement equipment based on technical methods and standards recognised by the United States Environmental Protection Agency to ensure the accuracy and reliability of their readings."
Arthur said the government understood that some areas did not have dedicated monitoring stations.
"In such cases, data from the nearest monitoring station will be used."
He added that the ministry would increase the number of monitoring stations to obtain more accurate readings.

Pressure to achieve academic and career success, relationship problems, social media influence and financial difficulties are among the main factors affecting young people's mental health.

Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the 2023 National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) found that 4.6 per cent of Malaysians aged 16 and above, or about one million people, suffered from depression.
Young people recorded the highest prevalence, at 7.9 per cent among those aged 16 to 19, and 7.6 per cent among those aged 20 to 29.

In a written parliamentary reply to Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (Pas-Tumpat), who asked about the mental well-being of young people, Dzulkefly said his ministry had established the National Centre of Excellence for Mental Health to coordinate government policies and initiatives on mental health.
The centre is responsible for addressing mental health crises, developing policies, implementing interventions and providing training.
Dzulkefly said the ministry also welcomed a proposal to establish an interministerial task force to pool expertise and strengthen early intervention.

Several cross-ministry initiatives were already in place, he said, including the Healthy Minds Programme with the Education Ministry and the Healthy Student Programme with the Higher Education Ministry.
He said the ministry also served as a referral centre for cases requiring further assessment through KafeTeen services under the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry.
Meanwhile, the 2022 NHMS, which assessed post-partum depression, found that 11.2 per cent of mothers experienced the condition, with nine in 10 unaware they had it.
Dzulkefly said post-partum depression was more prevalent among younger mothers and those living in urban areas.
He said families, friends and the wider community had a role in recognising signs of mental health issues among young people for early intervention and treatment.

ccbf122c07077f52: AUSTIN: Lewis Hamilton on Thursday welcomed Formula One’s decision to return to Africa, but revealed reservations over the choice of Rwanda to host the continent’s first Grand Prix in more than three decades.
The seven-time world champion also said he wanted to stay in F1 racing into his forties to make sure he can fulfil his dream of racing in an African Grand Prix.
Speaking to reporters ahead of this weekend’s United States Grand Prix, the Ferrari driver said he was aware of concerns regarding Rwanda and said they should not be overlooked.

"Of course, I don’t get to choose where we go and, naturally, there’s problems all over the world today,” he said. “I’ve seen many of the stories, but I think we really have to approach it with humility.”
Formula One announced a 10-year agreement to race in Rwanda last week with the race set to join the calendar after a circuit has been built in the early 2030s.
The last time an F1 race was held in Africa was the 33rd South African Grand Prix near Johannesburg in 1993 when Hamilton was just eight years old.
"There’s a lot that we don’t know,” added Hamilton who has called for a return to Africa for many years.
“Growing up in England, they never taught us anything about Africa. It needs to be on the curriculum…

a181882b563b5605: DETROIT: Versatile actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in Hollywood megahits including the sci-fi classic "Alien," the war comedy "M*A*S*H," and the action drama "Top Gun," has died at the age of 93.
Skerritt, a Detroit native whose Hollywood career spanned from the 1960s to the 2020s, died on Wednesday of natural causes, his family said in a statement.
"While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humor, curiosity, wisdom, generosity, and the love he brought into our lives," they said.
"He cared deeply about imagination, creativity, storytelling, service, veterans, the natural world, and helping others find and share their own voices," they added.
Known for his rugged good looks and ability to shine in a variety of genres, Skerritt delivered memorable performances in leading and supporting roles in film and television.

Skerritt's breakthrough role was a roguish US Army surgeon in director Robert Altman's 1970 Korean War black comedy "M*A*S*H," a film whose ensemble cast also included Donald Sutherland, Elliott Gould and Sally Kellerman.
Skerritt played Southerner Duke Forrest as the doctors at the Mobile Army Surgical Hospital stitched up wounded troops.
The film, whose popularity coincided with American unease over the Vietnam War, was nominated for five Academy Awards.

In director Ridley Scott's claustrophobic 1979 sci-fi horror "Alien," Skerritt played Dallas, the captain of an ill-fated spacecraft whose crew encounters a deadly parasitic extraterrestrial creature with a surrealist look and a bad attitude.
In the film's famous and bloody "chestburster" scene, Skerritt's character is seated next to castmate John Hurt when a baby alien violently exits the torso of Hurt's character.
"Alien," an influential masterpiece whose ensemble cast also included Sigourney Weaver and Ian Holm, earned two Oscar nominations.
"It is spontaneity and impulse that make the difference, and that is what I felt we had with 'Alien'.

"Every one of us had that immediate rapport with each other — the respect that I had for the other actors and the respect that they had for me," Skerritt told interviewer Peter Sobczynski in 2019, while also lauding Scott's directorial brilliance.
"Alien" was one of several films in which Skerritt appeared that featured strong female characters, in this case Weaver's courageous character Ripley. That was considered pioneering at the time.
"When I read the script, one of the things that I liked most about it was that the woman becomes the hero. I loved that," Skerritt said.

"The sight of women being in positions of strength and fortitude to make the right connections and decisions was what appealed to me. I experienced that as well in 'Steel Magnolias,' with the women in that. I liked the idea of women being tough and strong and influential," he added.
In "Steel Magnolias" (1989), Skerritt played Drum Eatenton, husband of Sally Field's M'Lynn Eatenton.

Tony Scott, the brother of the "Alien" director, cast Skerritt in the key supporting role of naval aviation instructor Viper Metcalf in the 1986 blockbuster "Top Gun" that helped star Tom Cruise soar into Hollywood's stratosphere.

Skerritt also played Shirley MacLaine's husband in director Herbert Ross's 1977 ballet drama "The Turning Point," and starred alongside another emerging star in Brad Pitt in Robert Redford's beautifully shot 1992 period drama "A River Runs Through It."

Among other films in which he appeared were: "Harold and Maude" (1971), "Ice Castles" (1978), "The Dead Zone" (1983), "Poltergeist III" (1988), "Contact" (1997), "Tears of the Sun" (2003) and "Ted" (2012).

On the small screen, Skerritt starred in the offbeat CBS series "Picket Fences" from 1992 to 1996, playing a Wisconsin town sheriff and claiming an Emmy as outstanding lead actor in a drama series in 1993.

Born on Aug 25, 1933, in Detroit, Skerritt served in the US Air Force before becoming an actor, making his film debut in 1962 alongside a young Redford in "War Hunt." He was a father of five children and was married three times.

712bc0d815dcfe0f: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI has less to do with which model you choose than with what you build around it.

That’s an important shift. For the past several years, much of the AI conversation has centered on model capability: bigger models, better reasoning, larger context windows, higher benchmark scores. Those advances have been extraordinary. But as AI moves from experimentation to production, the question facing enterprise leaders has changed—it’s no longer, “what can the model do?”—it’s now, “Can we deliver that intelligence reliably, economically, and at scale?”

Increasingly, the answer depends on the serving harness—the engineering system surrounding the model, including the architecture, memory management, scheduling, and optimization decisions that determine how efficiently model intelligence becomes a production capability.
For technical executives, that changes where AI investment should go—and what they should demand from the architecture supporting it.
Start with the workload, not the model
There is no universally “best” model or AI architecture. There is only the right solution for the business problem.

A customer-facing assistant optimized for fast responses has fundamentally different requirements from a document-processing pipeline that can run overnight. An internal knowledge application and a high-volume customer service platform may use the same foundation model but require very different serving architectures.
The workload defines the constraints. The constraints should determine the architecture.

That sounds simple, but it runs counter to the way many organizations have approached early AI deployments. During a proof of concept, model accuracy naturally dominates the discussion. Production introduces constraints that are much easier to ignore when only a handful of users are involved: latency, concurrency, memory pressure, GPU utilization, infrastructure cost, and unpredictable traffic.

A model that produces marginally better answers is not necessarily the better production choice if it doubles inference costs or cannot meet the application’s latency requirements. Not every workload needs a Ferrari. Sometimes the smarter engineering decision is the model that delivers exactly the performance the business needs without paying for capability it doesn’t.

The objective should be to deploy the right intelligence at the right cost for the workload. That makes serving architecture more than an engineering concern. It becomes an investment decision: where to spend on compute, where to optimize, and where additional model capability simply isn’t worth the cost.
Engineer the system, not the model

Once AI reaches production, seemingly isolated engineering decisions begin affecting one another. Serving architecture influences memory utilization. Memory management affects concurrency. Concurrency shapes batching and scheduling, and scheduling affects GPU utilization and latency.

Only then can techniques such as quantization, speculative decoding, or optimized attention mechanisms deliver their full value. This interdependence matters because organizations can spend considerably more on infrastructure without solving the constraint limiting performance.

GPU memory is a good example. During inference, the model’s weights remain fixed, but the key-value (KV) cache grows with active requests and context length. As concurrency increases, a system can run short of usable GPU memory even when compute capacity is still available. Adding more compute without understanding that bottleneck may simply make an inefficient system more expensive.

The lesson for technology leaders is broader than memory management: Measure before you optimize. Identify the dominant constraint. Address it. Measure the result. Then determine if another bottleneck emerged. Repeat.

Don’t think of optimization techniques as Pokémon cards: The goal isn’t to collect them all. The goal is to apply the technique that removes the highest-impact constraint while preserving the application’s business requirements.

For technology leaders, that demands a different governance question. Instead of asking which AI capabilities the organization can deploy, ask which constraints stand between a proven capability and sustainable business value.
Build for change, not today’s benchmark

Perhaps the most important reason to invest in the serving harness is that today’s leading model will probably not be tomorrow’s. Models will improve. Hardware will evolve. New optimization techniques will emerge. The architecture surrounding them should make those changes easier to absorb, not force the enterprise to rebuild its AI platform every time technology advances.
That makes adaptability an increasingly important outcome of AI strategy.

Organizations that build serving systems around workload requirements, clear service-level objectives, and measurable production economics gain the ability to evaluate new models and infrastructure against what the business actually needs. A model change can become an evaluation and configuration decision rather than an architectural reset.

EXL researchers have explored these production challenges in greater depth in the EXL Engineering the Harness series. It examines how serving architecture, memory management, scheduling, and inference optimization work together to make enterprise AI more efficient, scalable, and economically sustainable.
Increasingly, enterprises have access to many of the same models. Sustainable differentiation comes from how effectively an organization turns that intelligence into business outcomes.
The model provides the intelligence. The harness determines whether the enterprise can deliver outcomes reliably, economically, and at scale.
This content was produced by EXL. It was not written by MIT Technology Review’s editorial staff.

88e73b340e5cf3c4: As a child, you likely saw a few Disney movies depicting inanimate objects, such as clocks, cups, and toys, as interactive companions to humans — an act of pure magic, seemingly. But scientists at MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) are now doing something similar: transforming stationary items into self-aware tools that perceive and respond to human motion to complete a task. Engineers have 3D-printed these dynamic items with built-in sensing, using conductive materials for sensors and traces (sort of like wires) inside. The issue: both components were typically fabricated using the same material, so they’d emit similar signals. It’s sort of like hearing two radio stations at the same time, a mixup that’s hard to interpret. This confuses, say, a glove that relays instructions to a robotic hand about how to handle a specific object. The device couldn’t filter out the noise or verify the angle of a user’s motions, leading a humanoid student to make errors. Researchers at CSAIL and Tianjin University (TJU) in China may have found a way to 3D print more precise interactive items. With their “X-Hinges” software, users can customize a design, and the tool will automatically embed two different materials: a filament for the sensors designed to send the strongest signal possible, and another for the wire-like elements that don’t interfere. Interactions won’t get lost in translation, meaning users can fabricate objects that respond in real-time, such as small robots, household decor, object-detection systems, and toys. With X-Hinges, users can put together an item by selecting and connecting different shapes, then choosing how certain parts move. The item won’t be limited to moving in just one way like previous approaches; instead, users can select up to three “axes:” compressing, up and down, or to the sides. Building a robotic hand, for example, you’d likely want its fingertips to move vertically and laterally. The new tool would then embed sensors where the object bends (in this case, its joints) to capture motion data from both angles. That way, the device can understand and respond to your interactions more dynamically once it’s 3D-printed. “It’s kind of like adding a conscious element to everyday objects,” says Jiaji Li, MIT electrical engineering and computer science (EECS) postdoc and CSAIL researcher, who is a senior author on a paper introducing the work. “What you get is objects that better understand how they’re being used and have more ways to respond. In the same way an AI agent is programmed to make certain decisions based on our instructions, these creations have built-in sensing to adaptively react to human touch.” Jiaji Li and lead author Xiang Chang, a TJU PhD student and visiting researcher at CSAIL, used X-Hinges to create many clever devices. For example, they made a glove that can teach a robot how to grasp blocks. It adjusts to the size of a user’s hands, then records how the joints in their fingers bend via sensors before rapidly relaying that information to a humanoid hand to mimic it. The glove could be useful in factories or homes, where a robot often needs to learn new interactions quickly. The researchers also produced a small, origami-style lamp using X-Hinges. It senses when a human pinches it closed and adjusts its brightness accordingly. When you turn on this adaptive, portable light source (sort of like a reading light), it looks like a piece of folded-up paper that sprouts into a lamp. X-Hinges can even assemble devices that identify which objects have been placed on it. You could put a banana on top, for instance, and it’ll recognize the fruit almost immediately based on the tactile data it’s recorded using its sensors. This advanced physical awareness could be integrated into detection systems in places such as airports and grocery stores.  Behind each of the scientists’ creations is an easy-to-use interface that helps you design interactive objects from scratch. Users can choose how each part of their design looks and moves, just as the researchers did when making a video game controller that resembles a cartoon shark. X-Hinges gives you four shapes to choose from: a custom option, cylinder, rectangle, and thin outline. To recreate the unique look of a shark’s tail, the researchers designed their own shape. They then chose how the toy bent, opting for its tail to move up and down, sort of like a joystick. Finally, the program embedded the sensors, and the scientists 3D-printed their device. The researchers say that X-Hinges’ diverse motions are a novel feature compared to past attempts to 3D-print responsive everyday objects. “Most methods only allow for one axis of motion, often due to signal interference. X-Hinges enables your 3D-printed item to move from three angles,” says Chang. “Ultimately, you get a design with the intended movement you want. It also records motion data in each of those areas at the same time, making the device responsive to different kinds of interactions.” The tool could help realize the untapped potential of the seemingly mundane. Objects we use every day for a specific purpose, like a water bottle for drinking or a lamp for lighting, could become interactive gadgets. Much like how a chatbot uses a sort of digital intelligence to answer your prompts, an object could leverage a kind of physical intelligence to execute a physical task when users interact with it. For now, though, X-Hinges faces a calibration bottleneck. Each time an item is 3D-printed, its layout of electrical elements varies slightly, so two devices that appear identical from the outside may not make the same sensor readings. This is crucial if you’re building a deformable fitness glove, for instance, for two separate users. To fix this, Chang and Li built a computer vision system that can recalibrate outputs to align, ensuring data is accurate across two of the same items, although they hope to develop a built-in signal recalibration mechanism in the future. That ambition traces back to the throughline in Jiaji Li’s own research: letting actuation and sensing “grow” directly inside a 3D-printed object, instead of adding them on afterward. He previously built printed tendon-driven mechanisms that gave objects the ability to move; X-Hinges is how he’s now building on the ability to sense. The next step, he says, is combining the two in a single print — it’s actuation and sensing born together in the same fabrication process, opening the door to new physical platforms for embodied intelligence and AI agents. Chang and Li wrote the paper with MIT associate professor of EECS and CSAIL principal investigator Stefanie Mueller and recent TJU graduate Haiyang Yan. Their work was supported, in part, by a postdoctoral research fellowship from Zhejiang University and the MIT-GIST Program. The researchers will present their work at the ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology in early November.

55fbeed2b08e6c9f: A 25-year-old German experimental photographer has won the 2026 Nikon Small World photomicrography competition with a striking image of droplets of ink being deposited on paper by an inkjet printer. Ole Bielfeldt beat out 1,802 other entries hailing from 69 different countries.

Bielfeldt became interested in photomicrography during the COVID-19 lockdown after discovering an old microscope in his parents' attic. He figured out how to build an adaptor out of a tube and some wood to connect the microscope to his father's camera and taught himself the art through trial and error, building custom tools as needed. He documents how he captures transformative images of everyday objects with behind-the-scenes videos posted to macrofying, his photography and videography brand.

It was Bielfeldt's curiosity about the inner workings of inkjet printers that inspired his winning entry, but capturing the action of ink drops being deposited on paper was a challenge, given that the process happens so quickly. The droplets, for instance, moved faster than the camera's shutter speed. Bielfeldt's solution was to deconstruct the printer so that the paper moved under a stationary (rather than moving) printhead, and then take the image in a dark room, using a flash to serve as the shutter, thereby freezing the ink drops mid-air. There was no need for pricey equipment. Bielfeldt does not use AI in his images, preferring to rely on traditional techniques.

c3c91acfa9688b51: GitLab on Wednesday patched a maximum-severity flaw that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on self-managed servers under certain conditions. Affected software releases date back a full 12 years - so upgrade to a fixed version now.

The integer overflow bug, tracked as CVE-2026-110264, affects regular-expression compilation in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE), including versions dating back to GitLab 7.0, released in June 2014.

The flaw, “under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server due to integer overflow when compiling a specially crafted regular expression,” the vendor said in its release notes.

GitLab released fixes in versions 19.5.1, 19.4.3, and 19.3.6, and backported the patch to versions 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10, and 18.11.13. The vendor “strongly recommends” that all organizations running vulnerable software upgrade to a fixed version “as soon as possible.”

GitLab-managed infrastructure, including GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated, remains patched, and the vendor also released two threat detections (here and here) for customers with self-managed instances.
Bug hunter Johan Carlsson reported the vulnerability through GitLab’s HackerOne bug bounty program.

“For organizations running self-managed GitLab infrastructure, the potential impact is severe,” warned threat-detection firm SOC Prime. “GitLab repositories frequently contain source code, CI/CD configuration, deployment secrets, access tokens, infrastructure definitions, and connections to production environments. Server-level compromise could therefore create opportunities for credential theft, repository manipulation, supply chain attacks, persistence, or lateral movement.”
While there’s no indication - yet - of any in-the-wild exploitation attempts, we’d expect criminals to start scanning for vulnerable instances soon.

The ongoing PHP chaos may have given defenders a short head-start on this one, but considering the perfect 10 CVSS severity rating and GitLab’s reach into the enterprise - it claims 50 million registered users and more than 50 percent of the Fortune 100 - that’s not going to last long.

Last month, attackers started battering another max-severity flaw in the same GitLab CE and EE products just days after the vendor issued a patch, according to the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and private researchers.®

0aab0a15c7086a2d: After embarrassing reports revealed weak private keys, one of which was just a single digit, Indian certification authority eMudhra has decided to take the L and get out of the global SSL/TLS cert game entirely.

eMudhra announced Thursday that it was abandoning that arm of its business. Sure, the intense scrutiny heaped on the company was a factor, but the firm also argued that growing compliance costs and competition from free certificate providers had made the business increasingly difficult to justify.

“Global SSL/TLS is a small part of eMudhra’s business contributing to about 1 percent of the global revenue,” the company explained, noting that free SSL/TLS cert issuance from large firms and increased compliance and data sovereignty requirements have made it a minor part of the firm’s operation, and one that doesn’t merit so much bad press.

“The level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business,” eMudhra explained. “In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders.”
An argument could be made that, even if SSL/TLS accounts for just 1 percent of its global revenue, a private CA key with a value of 4 still deserves a thorough public shaming.

It’s only been two days since eMudhra’s weak private keys were exposed in public reports, following a report to Mozilla on October 17, and it wasn’t exactly hard for security researchers to recover them: The eight affected private-key values ranged from the number 4 (yes – a plain old number 4), to 56 and 66, to the far more complicated 115, 155, 156, 230, and 237.
No quantum computer required to crack those keys. Wow – better save the qubits.

This wasn’t just an embarrassing collection of numbers, either: The weak keys belonged to eight intermediate certificate authorities, potentially allowing attackers to forge certificates trusted by systems that hadn’t blocked them. eMudhra, however, maintains that the affected CAs had issued no end-entity certificates.

eMudhra quickly went on the defensive about its mind-boggling key-management failure, acknowledging the weak keys while pointing to independent audits and a problem during its key-generation ceremony that it said produced the weak keys alongside the intended strong ones.

“A flaw in the key generation ceremony caused a wrap/unwrap step to produce a second set of weak keys alongside the original strong keys,” the company said the day after the key fiasco was reported. “The weak keys were the ones published to the browser root stores.”

Despite that, eMudhra said the relevant certificate infrastructure had undergone two years of independent audits and had been in browser trust lists since mid-2025, raising questions about why the weak keys weren't caught sooner.

eMudhra claimed on Thursday that the affected CAs had issued no end-entity certificates, that it had revoked those CAs within 14 hours of discovering the issue, and that neither its infrastructure nor its data had been compromised as a result of its key boo-boo.

Still, the incident has given eMudhra another reason to shave off a small part of its business rather than continue facing scrutiny over its certificate operations. It’s still going to issue a root-cause report and fulfill its remaining commitments to browser root programs as it winds down the business.
The company said it’ll continue to serve G1 RSA roots until it transitions customers to other certificate issuers, which it will do free of charge.
“Revocation and certificate status services will keep running until every issued certificate has expired or been replaced,” the company said. ®

3d3eb883e72a4edc: WASHINGTON: A federal judge on Thursday ordered Donald Trump to sit for a deposition by Dec 11 in his US$10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC, which has accused the US president of stalling to avoid answering questions under oath, the Associated Press reported.

Representatives for Trump's legal team and the BBC did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Trump's lawsuit filed in December in Florida federal court accuses the BBC of intentionally misleading viewers into thinking he directed supporters to storm the US Capitol by splicing together different parts of a Jan 6, 2021 speech.
The BBC admitted the edits were misleading and apologised to Trump, though it denies being liable for defamation.

In court filings, the broadcaster has accused Trump and his lawyers of dragging their feet in response to their requests for records and other information that is exchanged between parties in a process known as discovery.
The BBC is seeking financial records from Trump's Mar-a-Lago club and the web of business entities associated with him, saying the information is necessary to defend against Trump's damages claims.

Trump's lawyers say the requests are too broad and irrelevant to the case. They have also denied in court filings that Trump is avoiding a deposition, saying Trump's duties and security needs must take precedence.

The edited speech appeared in a BBC "Panorama" documentary show shortly before the 2024 presidential election, which Trump won. A leaked internal BBC memo cited the edits as evidence of potential political bias, sparking a public relations crisis for the broadcaster and leading to high-level resignations.--REUTERS

2a056305b9bcd060: BANGKOK: Two Chinese Uyghur men detained in Thailand have received royal pardons and are awaiting deportation, a Thai official and an activist said on Thursday, though it was not yet clear where they will go.

The men are among the last of more than 300 members of the Muslim minority group held in Thailand in 2014, according to Kannavee Suebsang, a former Thai MP who was working for the UN Refugee Agency at the time and now runs an NGO. Almost all have been deported.

Around 170 women and children were sent to Turkiye in 2015, while two other groups were deported to China in 2015 and 2025, despite international condemnation of the treatment of the Uyghurs in the northwestern Chinese region of Xinjiang.
The two men were pardoned and on Wednesday transferred to Bangkok's Immigration Detention Centre, according to Thanit Thaiwatcharamat, deputy commander of Thailand's immigration bureau.
They will be deported to China or another country, pending the Thai government's decision, he told AFP.
The men arrived in Thailand in 2014 and were among five who tried to escape from immigration detention in 2020, Kannavee said.
Amnesty International said last year the men "described oppressive conditions of detention, including crowding and damp", as a reason for their escape.

They were subsequently convicted for the escape bid and jailed. The convictions ruled them out of previous deportations, Kannavee told AFP, adding that Thailand's National Security Council will now decide their future.
"They will have to consider different factors. For example, if another country is offering to host these men as well as China, this is the decision that needs to be made," he said.
Under Thai law, imprisoned foreign nationals can only be deported once their sentences are complete.
The remaining three men jailed for their 2020 escape attempt – whose situation has been highlighted by Amnesty International – are still in prison, the Thai official said.

Rights groups and Uyghurs overseas allege that China has detained more than a million Muslims, mostly Uyghurs, in a network of facilities in Xinjiang that are rife with violence, torture, forced labour, political indoctrination and other abuses.

Beijing vehemently denies the accusations, saying its policies in Xinjiang have eradicated extremism and boosted development, and that the facilities were voluntarily attended training centres that closed years ago after attendees "graduated."--AFP

Najib, 73, sedang menjalani hukuman penjara enam tahun di Penjara Kajang selepas Lembaga Pengampunan Wilayah Persekutuan memendekkan separuh tempoh hukuman asal 12 tahun pada Februari 2024. Denda awal sebanyak RM210 juta turut dikurangkan kepada RM50 juta.
Dia dipenjarakan pada Ogos 2022 selepas Mahkamah Persekutuan menolak rayuan akhirnya dalam kes SRC International Sdn Bhd.

Pada Disember 2025, Najib disabitkan atas kesalahan salah guna kuasa dan pengubahan wang haram membabitkan lebih RM2 bilion berkaitan 1MDB. Dia dijatuhi hukuman penjara 15 tahun serta didenda RM11.38 bilion, dan kini sedang merayu sabitan tersebut.

Awal tahun ini, ketua pesuruhjaya Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) ketika itu Azam Baki berkata, negara berupaya mendapatkan semula USD2 bilion (RM8.16 bilion) lagi aset yang dikaitkan dengan skandal 1MDB menjelang akhir tahun depan.
Azam berkata, aset-aset tersebut merupakan sebahagian baki dana terakhir yang telah diseleweng.
Setakat 2025, Malaysia telah memperoleh semula RM31.3 bilion, atau 74.53% daripada RM42 bilion dana yang diselewengkan daripada 1MDB.
901b9002176b3573: TOKYO: Governments and companies around the world shut down websites Thursday as they raced to protect themselves from hacks after artificial intelligence uncovered critical flaws in a widely used programming language called PHP.

PHP helps run about 70 per cent of the world's websites – from online stores and news outlets to government services – according to Wiz Research, one of the cybersecurity firms that found the two flaws.
Created in the early 1990s, PHP originally stood for "personal home page" but now means "hypertext preprocessor" and sits underneath popular web design platforms.
"These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history," a Wiz blog post said.
Increasingly powerful AI models can spot weak points in back-end computer code that have gone unnoticed by humans for years.
That has heightened cybersecurity fears, with the number of software vulnerabilities discovered worldwide in 2026 on track to roughly double last year's record total.
- 'QUITE DEVASTATING' -

PHP programmers released a fix Wednesday, and the US National Security Agency told organisations to patch their sites immediately or pull vulnerable systems offline – a call echoed by authorities from Japan to the European Union.
A platform affiliated with China's industry and information technology ministry urged the same, warning of "two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities with severe impact" in PHP.
Amazon Threat Intelligence said: "It remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information."
But Ryan Austin, who has worked on PHP issues for cybersecurity firm Calif, told the BBC: "at the moment, it doesn't look like exploitation has taken off or been widespread."

Only sites that run PHP on their own servers are exposed. Many large platforms are built on other programming languages or use operators that could install the fix quickly and were able to stay online.
Rahat Masood, senior lecturer in cybersecurity at the University of New South Wales, Sydney, described the discovery as "quite devastating."
It could allow "attackers to get into your servers without any authorisation, without any username or password", she told AFP.
"Once they are in the servers, they can do anything they want" – from stealing sensitive information to modifying website content – she added, urging institutions to "take it seriously."
- 'NEW PHASE' -

Government agency sites in countries from Australia to Finland, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom were among those that went dark. Services from insurance firms, transport operators and media outlets were down for emergency maintenance.

Popular apps, including a Pokemon sleep tracker, were also temporarily taken offline while the fix was implemented, while the foundation that runs Wikipedia warned users they could see outages while it addressed the flaws.
"If you run PHP, it is imperative that you update now," the PHP Foundation, which funds developers working on the language, said in a blog post.

Volker Dusch, a security engineer at the foundation, told the Wall Street Journal it was the most serious problem PHP had faced in more than a decade, comparing it to Heartbleed, a 2014 flaw that set off a worldwide rush to patch.
Security firm Calif found the flaws in August using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model, as part of an OpenAI-funded audit of PHP's code.
OpenAI said the discovery "marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact."
Wiz, which is owned by Google, said it found them independently weeks later with help from AI models including Google's Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol.
The flaws had been reported privately to PHP's developers and kept confidential while a fix was prepared.
- AI FUELS URGENCY -
Details leaked online Tuesday, a day before the planned release of the fix – prompting the rush to take sites offline before hackers could exploit them.

Steve Kerrison, senior lecturer in cybersecurity at the Singapore campus of James Cook University, told AFP that the fear of hackers using AI to quickly and easily exploit the PHP vulnerabilities had fuelled urgency to react.

So far there has been little evidence of damaging attacks, although data breaches could lead to a wave of so-called "phishing" attacks, where hackers use personal details to steal passwords, down the line.
Larger institutions, from government agencies to news outlets, should be able to fix their websites relatively fast, Kerrison said – but others may be left vulnerable.
"There are sites, systems and people out there who will have no idea about this and still won't for days, weeks and months," Kerrison warned.
That may include user-run blogs that could be weaponised to spread computer viruses, spam people or distribute malicious content, he said.--AFP

7dab5ebe3ff3f226: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's net financial burden from 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) is estimated at RM20.1 billion, assuming no further recovery of funds or assets, the Finance Ministry (MoF) said.
The figure is based on the government's total financial obligations related to 1MDB of RM51.4 billion, less RM31.3 billion in recovered funds and assets.

"Since the government began assuming the debt obligations and financial commitments related to 1MDB in April 2017, it has settled payments totalling RM42.5 billion, comprising RM27.7 billion in principal payments, and RM14.8 billion in interest and other commitments," MoF said in a written parliamentary reply.

He was responding to a question from Lee Chuan How (PH-Ipoh Timor) regarding new mechanisms to ensure that liabilities similar to those of 1MDB are not shifted onto taxpayers, as well as assurances that the claims process will not be compromised by developments concerning the criminal sentencing of the perpetrators.
Regarding efforts to recover funds, the MoF affirmed that the government remains committed to pursuing claims and asset recovery efforts related to 1MDB.
"Any developments concerning criminal sentencing or the granting of a pardon to an individual do not, in themselves, terminate civil claims aimed at recovering misappropriated funds.
"Civil claims have a different basis of action and evidentiary process compared to criminal proceedings," the ministry said.
MoF said the implications of any decision regarding sentencing or a pardon under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution must be examined based on the scope of that decision and the applicable laws.

"The right of the government and 1MDB to pursue civil claims should be assessed based on the grounds for the claims, the evidence, and the court orders within those proceedings; meanwhile, any asset forfeiture action is subject to the legal provisions and conditions that govern such measures.

"The government's stance is firm: efforts to recover state funds will continue through available legal channels, while respecting the jurisdiction of the courts and the power of pardon as provided for under the Federal Constitution," the ministry said.
It said the government's priority is to maximise the recovery of funds to settle 1MDB's obligations, reduce the nation's financial burden, and safeguard the interests of the people.
6d6b0007f22596fa: PETALING JAYA: Barisan Nasional dan PAS akan berkongsi pentas untuk mengumumkan calon masing-masing bagi PRN Melaka, kata Pengerusi BN Zahid Hamidi.

34d7d30096cca162: JERUSALEM: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing small right-wing parties to withdraw from next week's tight election over fears they could siphon off votes.
Ahead of the Oct 27 election, polls show Netanyahu's right-wing bloc neck and neck with that of his main centre-right rival Gadi Eisenkot.
The main target of Netanyahu's push has been Ofer Winter, founder of the new far-right Amcha Israel party, which is polling around the 3.25 per cent electoral threshold needed to enter parliament.
Should they fail to clear the bar, tens of thousands of right-wing votes would be lost.

On Thursday, Netanyahu posted an image on X depicting Winter smiling while burning votes, with a caption warning that voting for parties below the electoral threshold would cause a coalition of opposition parties to win power.
Netanyahu and a key coalition partner, hawkish Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, have for days accused Winter of endangering their bloc's chances and sought to convince him to abandon his candidacy.
On Tuesday, the two met with Winter's spiritual mentor, Rabbi Eli Sadan, in an apparent bid to increase pressure on the retired commander.
A day later, Smotrich went public with an offer, promising Winter a ministerial post in the next government if he agreed to drop out of the race.
Winter had initially pledged to support a future Netanyahu-led coalition on condition it advance the conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jewish men.
The issue has become increasingly contentious as the military grapples with manpower shortages while most ultra-Orthodox men continue to receive exemptions from compulsory service.
But Winter has resisted calls to step aside. On Wednesday, he said it "may not have been right" to announce his support for Netanyahu in advance, but has vowed not to support Eisenkot.

Netanyahu has also reportedly sought the withdrawal of Moti Leitner, founder of a new ultra-Orthodox party that aims to challenge the dominance of two established ultra-Orthodox factions allied with the prime minister.
Israeli media reported that Netanyahu met Leitner on Tuesday to urge him to quit the race, but the young politician refused.
Although his party is polling well below the electoral threshold, it could still attract tens of thousands of religious voters who might otherwise back Netanyahu's traditional allies.

Earlier this week, another small party dropped out of the race. Benny Gantz announced he was withdrawing from the election after opinion polls consistently showed his Blue and White party far below the threshold.

Gantz was Netanyahu's principal rival in the 2019 and 2020 elections before serving alongside him in national unity governments during the Covid-19 pandemic and after the outbreak of the war in 2023.--aFP
b28b717251c37d86: The PHP2Shell security fiasco has forced 32 UK government services offline and left another four partially unavailable as Whitehall scrambles to patch the critical vulnerabilities wreaking havoc across the web.
The figures were disclosed in the House of Lords on Thursday, where tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra outlined the disruption following the discovery of two critical flaws in PHP.

"Currently, the information I have is that 32 government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," Lloyd told peers. "That has resulted largely from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied."
"We are working very carefully with departments to restore the services safely and securely following that remediation activity," she added.

Whitehall has not published a full list of affected services, although the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) is among those known to have taken their websites offline, rather inconveniently with next week's Budget looming. Peers also raised reports of disruption affecting the DVLA and police services.

Britain isn't alone in pulling the plug. Government websites in Germany, France, Belgium, Finland, and the Netherlands have also been taken offline as a precaution, along with Australia's own cybersecurity agency website. Across the Atlantic, the NSA has urged organizations to patch or disconnect vulnerable systems, although the US government has not publicly confirmed any website shutdowns.

PHP2Shell comprises two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on vulnerable servers. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) warned organizations to patch immediately or consider pulling affected systems offline until they could be fixed.

"The NCSC was briefed by OpenAI last week on this potential specific vulnerability and has been working to ensure that disclosure happened in a co-ordinated way with vendors, so there was sufficient preparation to protect customers," Lloyd said.

Security firm Calif found one of the PHP bugs using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model, while Google's Wiz separately uncovered both flaws with the help of AI tools. OpenAI then dug into the vulnerabilities itself and worked with vendors and government agencies to get the word out.
The government established a cross-departmental incident response operation before public disclosure, Lloyd said. The NCSC also sent 50,000 warnings to businesses and other organizations.

The disruption has spread beyond central government. Liberal Democrat peer Baroness Ludford pointed to several councils whose services had reportedly been taken offline, including Edinburgh, Oxford, Bristol, Lambeth, and Barnet.

She questioned why central government and local authorities remain outside the statutory duties proposed under the government's Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, which returns to the Lords on Monday.

"We are not currently aware of any confirmed compromise of central government systems resulting from these vulnerabilities," Lloyd told peers, later extending that assessment to the wider UK public sector.
AWS says attackers were exploiting the flaws four days before they were publicly disclosed, while Cloudflare has since recorded millions of attempts to weaponize them. ®
